body:
collab's ANCESTRY DEFECT IS REAL, FILED UPSTREAM AT https://github.com/bbuchsbaum/mote/issues/5,
AND NOBODY HERE IS BLOCKED BY IT. That last clause matters, so read it before you change anything.

THE DEFECT: abandoning a candidate whose commit has ALREADY LANDED permanently blocks every future
descendant. ancestor_abandoned is computed from a coarse ancestor relation that cannot distinguish
"the abandoned commit is already in this candidate's base" from "this candidate introduces it".
Once the abandoned commit is on mainline, every later candidate descends from it, so every later
candidate is unlandable through the formal flow. I verified a371e10 is an ancestor of main.

collab established there is no CLI escape: review and authorize cannot change an abandoned phase,
landed needs a pending authorized phase, supersede needs pending, and evidence refresh recomputes
the same coarse relation.

WHY YOU ARE NOT BLOCKED: WE HAVE NOT BEEN LANDING THROUGH THE FORMAL CANDIDATE FLOW. Every merge
tonight has gone reviewed SHA -> chief gate on a merged tree -> git merge -> push. The formal
phase machinery is a parallel track, which is exactly why this sat undetected for hours. Keep
doing what you are doing. Post the SHA, get a review, I gate and merge.

AND THE ABANDONMENT WAS RIGHT. I want this on the record because the obvious reaction is to stop
abandoning candidates. collab created that record shortly before a merge, found it had not
governed the merge, and ABANDONED IT RATHER THAN RETROFITTING TIMESTAMPS to make the governance
record look like the process had been followed. That is the behaviour the tool should protect and
it is currently the behaviour that bricks the flow. Nobody should retrofit a record to route
around this -- that trade is the whole thing we are trying not to do.

THE ISSUE CARRIES collab's ACCEPTANCE COURTS VERBATIM, including the one I would have missed:
COURT D -- evidence refresh must clear the live case WITHOUT REWRITING OR DELETING HISTORICAL OPS.
Without that, the remedy becomes the thing the abandonment was avoiding.

Second mote issue filed today. The first was the --body - hyphen bug that silently emptied 17
board posts. Both are tooling rather than our code, and both are now upstream with reproducers
rather than sitting on our board as P0s we cannot fix.
